newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-U.S. SWEEPS JAPAN 5-0 IN FED CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-U.S. SWEEPS JAPAN 5-0 IN FED CUP.

text.p: The United States erased all suspense early as Lindsay Davenport beat Japan's Ai Sugiyama in Sunday's opening match to clinch a Fed Cup World Group One playoff Sunday at Longwood Cricket Club.

Davenport's 6-4 7-6 (7-1) win, combined with its two singles victories on Saturday, gave the United States an insurmountable 3-0 lead in the best-of-five competition. The Americans went on to a 5-0 victory by taking the day's second singles match and the doubles.
The victory qualified the United States for World Group One contention in 1998. The Americans were upset by the Netherlands 3-2 in February in this year's championship competition.

"It's nice to get it done early," said U.S. team captain Martina Navratilova. "Lindsay was a little in and out today, but when I told her to do something, she did it. Seems like she was a little too serious today.
"Lindsay's game is to blast, but I'd like to see her vary her game a little more. It was like she was just playing well enough to win."
Davenport, ranked seventh in the world, trailed 3-1 in the first set and 4-2 in the second, but always seemed to have both the forcing groundstrokes and the confidence to recover.

"We were all so relaxed and happy after yesterday's 2-0 start, but I just felt flat when I got out here today," said Davenport. "When you win and still not play well, maybe that's a good sign for me."

Davenport's velocity off the forehand played a big part in the first set. Down 1-3, she broke Sugiyama in the next game and in the ninth game she broke again at 15-40 to go up 5-4. Serving with the wind, the Californian wrapped up the first set with the loss of only one point.

Davenport got even at 4-4 in the second set and forced a tiebreaker, in which she took the first four points. By this time Sugiyama, who had a trainer looking at her slightly twisted ankle a few games earlier, appeared to have no answers.
"Lindsay hit the ball so deep I really had no chances to be aggressive," said the 34th-ranked Sugiyama. "If I don't hit the ball deep, I have no chance.
"I'm not happy with the results, but I felt we tried our best," said Sugiyama.
Kimberly Po beat Naoko Sawamatsu 6-2 6-4 in the last singles and in the doubles, Davenport and Po beat Naoko Kijimuta and Nana Miyagi 6-4 6-4.
Po, ranked 15th in the world, was a late replacement for 13th-ranked Mary Joe Fernandez, who complained of wrist problems.
